prize_parts.citation: for the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks

statement.case_for: Optical lattice clocks are the clearest case on the shortlist of a cleanly originated idea (Katori's magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms in a Lamb-Dicke regime) that was turned into a new regime of measurement (Ye's strontium clocks at the 1e-18 level, with many-body and gravitational-redshift physics on top). It has been reproduced and surpassed in many laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, SYRTE, NIST) with mutual agreement at the 1e-18 level, so the robustness and reproducibility questions I always ask are answered. The credit is compact and fits two laureates, the work is separate from the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize, and the discovery rather than an application is what is being rewarded. In my opening ballot I ranked circuit QED first, but I rank a prize by how well it survives the committee's scrutiny and not by how close it is to my own field, and B014 now has the broadest and most scientifically argued support of any candidate.
statement.case_against: The redefinition of the SI second has not yet happened, so some of the impact is still prospective, and a sceptic could say the lattice clock is a refinement of a precision-measurement lineage already honoured in 1989, 2005 and 2012. The credit also leaves out contributors such as Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow, Takamoto and Hollberg-era groups, and the pairing leans on a judgement that Katori's idea and Ye's realisation are the decisive pair. The strongest honest reservation is that supporters (including me) may be rating this high partly because it is the safest, least contested option and not the most scientifically transformative one.

responses.point: Kroll ranks B014 first as the clearest case of a measurement technique opening new observations, and ranks B009 only seventh because a prize so soon after the 2025 circuit-based prize looks less timely.
responses.response: I agree on B014 and I accept his point about B009 more than my opening ballot suggested. The 2025 prize already established that superconducting circuits are quantum devices in the macroscopic-tunnelling sense, and circuit QED, though distinct (strong light-matter coupling and dispersive readout), will read to many outside the committee as the same story continuing. I still think the scientific case is real, but I disagree that it is weak, so I would keep B009 as an alternative and not drop it. Where I also differ from Kroll is that I would not call lattice clocks a decisive coherence demonstration only; the new physics I value is the many-body and gravitational-redshift regime Ye's clocks opened.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks B014 first because the lattice clock combines the magic-wavelength idea with ultranarrow forbidden transitions, which controls quantum projection noise and Doppler/recoil shifts together. She also finds the three-person cut leaves out Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow and others.
responses.response: Her argument on the Lamb-Dicke regime is the scientific reason I trust this as a genuine conceptual step. On attribution I think she is right that others are left out, but unlike the Higgs or IceCube entries the invention here has a clear originator (Katori, 2001-2003) and a clear leader of the performance frontier (Ye), so the two-name cut is defensible, and I would want the citation to say invention and realisation, so that it does not read as credit for the whole clock community. I also differ with her ranking of B008: the Cirac-Zoller-Blatt entry overlaps the 2012 prize more than she implies, and I would not elevate it above B016.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks the topological insulator entry B016 first as a new class of states characterised by topology, with a natural theory-plus-experiment pairing in Kane-Mele and Molenkamp, though he notes the HgTe proposal is outside the credited names.
responses.response: I agree B016 is conceptually the deepest candidate and I rank it fourth only because of attribution and prior recognition, not because of doubt about the physics. The missing Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal is the serious problem: Molenkamp's experiment tested a prediction by people who are not on the list, and Zhang is deceased. I would not call that fatal for the Kane-Mele theory, but I think it makes B016 harder to defend as a clean prize than B014. It is my second alternative, and I would support it if the committee decides that conceptual originality outweighs allocation tidiness.

responses.point: Pearce ranks the IceCube entry B021 first as a detector-driven discovery that opened high-energy neutrino astronomy, and ranks B014 third as a compact, original invention.
responses.response: I defer to him and to Danielsson on astroparticle physics, since this is outside my competence, and I take seriously that the diffuse flux is secure. My reservation is the one he flags himself: the credit is spread over a large collaboration and AMANDA-era pioneers, and source identification is still partial, so I would not fix this year's prize on it. If the committee is looking for a second part, I could not support adding it to a configuration with B014 unless the three-person limit is respected, which a union of five names would not be.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards optical lattice clocks as a discovery in the sense of the statutes, or as a metrological invention whose full impact depends on the not-yet-decided redefinition of the second.
Whether Katori and Ye are the right pair, given contributions from Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow, Takamoto and others and whether Hall and Haensch frequency-comb credit already covers part of the story.
How much weight the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits should have against a circuit QED prize, which I cannot judge impartially.
I rely on recollection for the exact chronology of Katori's proposal versus the first lattice-clock demonstrations and have not checked it against papers.
statement.conflict_note: Specific connection: I am Director of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology and a theorist in the Chalmers superconducting-circuit community, with close professional ties to groups working on circuit QED, so B009 (Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf) and, to a lesser extent, B008 should be treated with recusal in mind, and I have tried to discount my first-place ranking of B009 for that reason. No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B014, B016, B017, B021, B042, B001, B018 or B020.
